chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Fazari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Verily, there may be a family that is dutiful [to their elders], so their wealth grows, even if they are sinful.'
ai.seo_question: How does kindness to parents affect wealth in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* underscores the Shia concept of *birr* (piety/kindness) as a divine mechanism for sustenance, suggesting that familial righteousness can compensate for individual moral shortcomings. It highlights the communal nature of spiritual merit in Shia tradition, where the collective virtue of the household influences material provision, a theme often linked to the blessings of maintaining kinship ties (*silat al-rahim*).

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abū Muḥammad al-Fazārī, who heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) saying, “
The Messenger of Allah (ṣ) said, ‘Verily there may be a family that is dutiful [to their elders], so their wealth grows, even if they are sinful.’”
